title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 23
summary: Issued at 200 PM MST Fri Oct 02 2026 000 WTPZ43 KNHC 022031 TCDEP3 Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number 23 NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL EP182026 200 PM MST Fri Oct 02 2026 The structure of Rachel has not changed appreciably since the previous advisory. A ragged, cloud-filled eye can still be seen on visible satellite imagery. The cloud pattern can also be described as having a large central dense overcast or embedded center, with the deep convection spanning roughly 200 n mi in diameter. The latest subjective intensity estimate from TAFB is T4.5/77 kt, and the latest objective estimates from UW-CIMSS range from about 77-99 kt. The initial intensity is lowered slightly to 90 kt for this advisory, as a compromise of the subjective and objective estimates. The cyclone is still moving slowly westward at 265/4 kt and has made its closest approach Socorro Island, passing about 30 to 35 n mi north of the station, which recorded winds of 53 kt gusting to 74 kt and a minimum pressure 982.6 mb.
